findings.body:
Both admin handlers no longer wrap through `middleware.RequireRole("admin")`. Anyone who can reach the server can call `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` with no admin role check — broken authorization on user listing and role edits.

Restore the middleware on the v2 subrouter handles:

```suggestion
	v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
	v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

(Also keep `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` above the subrouter.)

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes admin authorization from both privileged endpoints while relocating them under `/api/v2`.

## What went wrong

The PathPrefix move to `/api/v2` is fine as versioning cleanup, but the diff also drops `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` and registers bare `http.HandlerFunc` handlers. After merge, `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` are reachable without the admin role check that previously wrapped them.

There is no other middleware or route-level guard in this tree that would restore that protection.

## Required fix

Keep the subrouter, restore the authz wrapper on both handles:

```go
authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")
v2 := r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()
v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removed `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` when moving admin routes under `/api/v2`; both handlers are now registered as bare `http.HandlerFunc` with no role check, so privileged user-list and role-edit endpoints are unauthenticated at the router layer.
